title: Name radius, diameter and circumference and construct a circle from a given radius or diameter

lesson.title: Meet the Circle: Radius, Diameter, and Circumference

steps.say: You already know how to use a protractor to measure and draw angles, so you are great at handling shapes carefully. Today we are just naming the three parts of a circle, and learning how to draw a circle when someone tells you one measurement.

visual.caption: A circle with its radius drawn

steps.say: Picture a basketball hoop from above, or the lid of a hot chocolate cup. Every circle starts with a middle point called the centre. The radius is the distance from the centre out to the edge, like one spoke on a bike wheel. Here the radius is four centimetres.

Now the diameter. That is the distance all the way across the circle, straight through the centre, edge to edge. It is made of two radiuses back to back, so the diameter is always double the radius. If the radius is four centimetres, the diameter is eight centimetres. And the circumference? That is the distance all the way around the outside, like walking one full lap around a round skating rink.

visual.caption: Radius 4 cm, so diameter is 8 cm across

steps.say: Let us construct one. Your friend says, draw a circle with a diameter of ten centimetres. Your compass opens to the radius, not the diameter, so first cut ten in half. Ten divided by two is five. So you set your compass to five centimetres, put the point on your centre dot, and spin one full turn. Done.

visual.caption: Compass set to 5 cm gives a 10 cm wide circle

steps.say: Here is the mix-up almost everyone makes. People grab the radius when the question is really about the diameter. Say a round garden bed has a radius of three metres. Someone writes, the way around is pi times three. That is wrong, because the going around measurement compares to the whole way across, not just half of it. The way across here is six metres, not three. So before you use any circle rule, always ask yourself, do I have half of the circle or the whole width?

visual.caption: Radius 3 m, but all the way across is 6 m

steps.say: So remember: the radius goes from the centre to the edge, the diameter goes all the way across through the centre and is double the radius, and the circumference is the whole lap around the outside.

lesson.answer: Radius is centre to edge, diameter is twice the radius straight across, and circumference is the lap all the way around.

practice.question: A round pizza at a Vancouver pizzeria has a diameter of thirty centimetres. What is its radius? And if you set a compass to draw that pizza on paper, what would you open the compass to?
practice.answer: The radius is fifteen centimetres, because thirty divided by two is fifteen. You would open the compass to fifteen centimetres, since a compass is always set to the radius.
